title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover tuning to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Priya Natarajan
description:
Motivation: Production workloads observed increased paging and KV-cache fragmentation under long-lived chat sessions and mixed sequence-length workloads. Paging spikes lead to tail-latency regressions and higher egress to disk on Dedicated nodes. This PR implements an adaptive eviction and spillover tuning strategy to reduce fragmentation, defer unnecessary paging, and prioritize eviction/compaction based on live fragmentation and access patterns.

Summary of changes: Implemented adaptive eviction priority that combines recency, fragment size, and coalescing potential; introduced a spillover pacing controller to smooth page-outs; added a background compaction coordinator that schedules defrag and compaction during idle windows; exposed fragmentation and spillover telemetry; made the continuous-batcher aware of in-flight KV-cache compaction to avoid scheduling large batches that increase memory pressure. Includes correctness tests, unit tests, and performance benchmarks.

Key goals: reduce paging frequency, reduce end-to-end tail latency for generation, lower overall disk spillover bytes, and avoid compaction-induced latency spikes.

Benchmarks: microbench on p4d instance with mixed short/long sequences showed: median token latency -3%, 95th percentile latency -18%, paging bytes reduced by 62% under sustained 95th percentile load; end-to-end throughput maintained within 2% of baseline. Canary on Dedicated cluster (10 nodes) showed a 40% reduction in page-out events and eliminated the pathological paging loops we observed in previous incidents.

Rollout & safety: feature gated behind runtime flag kv.adaptive_eviction.v2; staged rollout: developer canary -> 5% production -> 25% -> full. Telemetry dashboards and alerts added for paging_rate, fragmentation_ratio, compaction_time, and eviction_retries. If paging_rate increases above baseline+25% or compaction_time causes request latency regression, automatic rollback via routing policy is configured.

Breaking changes / compatibility: No API changes. Behavior changes are internal to runtime memory manager. Flag can be disabled for immediate rollback.

Related: builds on prior work in kv-cache defrag scheduler (ENG-270) and spillover coordinator (ENG-315). See linked Linear items.

Testing performed: unit tests for eviction correctness, integration test for spillover pacing under synthetic workload, stress test for compaction coordinator across multiple model sizes, canary run on Dedicated cluster, and benchmark harness results attached.

Notes: kept diffs focused to runtime/kv_cache and scheduler surface; avoided touching public API surface. This PR intentionally defers aggressive compaction heuristics (v3) to follow-up once we collect more field telemetry.
